```{r}
#I will create the outcome variable for low performance first in case 8
#I only keep students with an observed Case 8 score
analysis_data <- student_wide |>
  filter(!is.na(score_pct_case_c8))

#Bottom 20% cutoff for Case 8 performance
cutoff_case8 <- quantile(analysis_data$score_pct_case_c8,
                         probs = 0.20,
                         na.rm = TRUE)

#Binary outcome: Yes = student is in the bottom 20% on Case 8
analysis_data <- analysis_data |>
  mutate(
    low_perf_c8 = if_else(score_pct_case_c8 <= cutoff_case8, "Yes", "No"),
    low_perf_c8 = factor(low_perf_c8, levels = c("No", "Yes")))

#I'll check the prevalence of the outcome
mean(analysis_data$low_perf_c8 == "Yes")
table(analysis_data$low_perf_c8)
```

```{r}
#to create the new predictors in the database
#I'll use some functions because we'll use certain windows
#of data, like from case 1 to 3 so we can make this early prediction model

#also, we need new variables as the variables in the dataset are not
#fully independent

#function to obtain the last observed score of a student
last_observed_fn <- function(x) {
  vals <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(vals) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  vals[length(vals)]
}

#function to see if the scores of the student go up or down
score_slope_fn <- function(x) {
  idx <- which(!is.na(x))
  vals <- x[idx]
  if (length(vals) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  coef(lm(vals ~ idx))[2]
}

#function to compute the difference in recent scores
recent_change_fn <- function(x) {
  vals <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(vals) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  vals[length(vals)] - vals[length(vals) - 1]
}

#now we'll create the window data depending on how many cases
#we want to consider as the early performance
#I'm not sure if we want the first 3 or 5 so with a function
#we can change this later
make_window_data <- function(data, last_case) {
  score_vars   <- paste0("score_pct_case_c", 1:last_case)
  attempt_vars <- paste0("attempted_case_c", 1:last_case)

  #this is to not consider cases with no conversation with patient
  enabled_cases <- intersect(1:last_case, c(1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8))
  msg_vars  <- paste0("student_messages_case_c", enabled_cases)
  time_vars <- paste0("conversation_seconds_case_c", enabled_cases)

  #this creates the attempt variables only for conversation-enabled cases
  attempt_conv_vars <- paste0("attempted_case_c", enabled_cases)

  #now we can keep all variables of the cases as matrices
  score_mat   <- as.matrix(data[, score_vars])
  attempt_mat <- as.matrix(data[, attempt_vars])
  msg_mat     <- as.matrix(data[, msg_vars, drop = FALSE])
  time_mat    <- as.matrix(data[, time_vars, drop = FALSE])
  attempt_conv_mat <- as.matrix(data[, attempt_conv_vars, drop = FALSE])

  #number of conversation-enabled cases actually attempted
  attempted_conv_cases <- rowSums(attempt_conv_mat, na.rm = TRUE)

  #now the output which is a tibble with student ID and the outcome
  #which is the new variable low_perf_c8 classification
  out <- tibble(
    student_id = data$student_id,
    low_perf_c8 = data$low_perf_c8,

    #attempt summary to know how many cases are in the window
    #so we know participation of the student in the class
    attempted_total = rowSums(attempt_mat, na.rm = TRUE),

    #score summaries
    mean_score = rowMeans(score_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_score = apply(score_mat, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_observed_score = apply(score_mat, 1, last_observed_fn),
    score_slope = apply(score_mat, 1, score_slope_fn),
    recent_score_change = apply(score_mat, 1, recent_change_fn),

    #total conversational activity up to this point
    total_messages = rowSums(msg_mat, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_conversation_seconds = rowSums(time_mat, na.rm = TRUE),

    #number of conversation-enabled cases actually attempted
    attempted_conv_cases = attempted_conv_cases,

    #mean conversational activity conditional on attempted
    #conversation-enabled cases only.
    mean_messages = if_else(
      attempted_conv_cases > 0,
      rowSums(msg_mat, na.rm = TRUE) / attempted_conv_cases,
      NA_real_),
    mean_conversation_seconds = if_else(
      attempted_conv_cases > 0,
      rowSums(time_mat, na.rm = TRUE) / attempted_conv_cases,
      NA_real_))

  #to make sure all NAs are handled consistently
  out <- out |>
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, .x)))
  return(out)
}
```

```{r}
#we have missing data in some students
#some students may have missing score-based summaries
#I'll impute using medians from the training set only so we can have complete data

#I'll use a function to do this for reproducibility
median_impute_from_train <- function(train, test, outcome_name = "low_perf_c8") {
  predictor_names <- setdiff(names(train), c("student_id", outcome_name))
  for (v in predictor_names) {
    med_v <- median(train[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
    if (is.na(med_v)) {
      med_v <- 0
    }
    train[[v]][is.na(train[[v]])] <- med_v
    test[[v]][is.na(test[[v]])] <- med_v
  }
  list(train = train, test = test)
}
```

```{r}
#Again, to save time in the future if we get more data or update datasets,
#here we'll have 2 functions, one for computing performance metrics
#and another one for modeling and testing

get_metrics <- function(prob, pred, truth, model_name, threshold_used) {
  #prob is predicted probabilities of yes
  #pred is the predicted classes yes or no
  #true the true observed outcome
  #the confusion matrix needs the predicted classes and the truth
  cm <- confusionMatrix(pred, truth, positive = "Yes")
  tibble(
    model = model_name,
    threshold_used = threshold_used,
    share_flagged = mean(pred == "Yes"), #to know how many students are flagged
    #as at risk
    accuracy = as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    sensitivity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
    specificity = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
    precision = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]),
    balanced_accuracy = as.numeric(cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]),
  )
}

#function to fit models and evaluate them with the test dataset
fit_and_evaluate_models <- function(train_df, test_df) {
#first, we'll take out student_id to avoid issues
  #I already tried and generated issues being present as a predictor
  train_model <- train_df |>
    select(-student_id)
  test_model <- test_df |>
    select(-student_id)
#First model: logistic regression
  logit_model <- glm(low_perf_c8 ~ .,
                     data = train_model,
                     family = binomial)
  #now we extract the predicted probabilities instead of keeping log-odds
  #for easier interpretation
  prob_train_logit <- predict(logit_model, newdata = train_model, type = "response")
  prob_test_logit  <- predict(logit_model, newdata = test_model, type = "response")
  #the threshold will be in this case 0.80 so 20% high risk students
  #will be flagged as yes, from the training set
  threshold_logit <- quantile(prob_train_logit, probs = 0.80, na.rm = TRUE)
  #now we compute in the testing dataset the class Yes No using the threshold
  pred_test_logit <- factor(ifelse(prob_test_logit >= threshold_logit, "Yes", "No"),
                            levels = c("No", "Yes"))

#Second model: Naive Bayes
  nb_model <- naiveBayes(low_perf_c8 ~ .,
                         data = train_model)
  #I'm not sure here as the assumption is independence and some of the predictors
  #have dependencies
  #we compute now the predicted probabilities for both datasets based on the model
  prob_train_nb <- predict(nb_model, newdata = train_model, type = "raw")[, "Yes"]
  prob_test_nb  <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_model, type = "raw")[, "Yes"]
  #now the threshold that is basically the same as the previous model
  threshold_nb <- quantile(prob_train_nb, probs = 0.80, na.rm = TRUE)
  #with the threshold we compute now the class yes no in the testing dataset
  pred_test_nb <- factor(ifelse(prob_test_nb >= threshold_nb, "Yes", "No"),
                         levels = c("No", "Yes"))

#Third model: decision tree
  set.seed(1234)
  #we'll train with cv
  mycontrol <- trainControl(method = "cv",
                            number = 10,
                            classProbs = TRUE)
  #here's the tree
  tree_model <- train(low_perf_c8 ~ .,
                      data = train_model,
                      trControl = mycontrol,
                      method = "rpart",
                      tuneLength = 100)
  #now we predict probabilities in test and train data based on the tree
  prob_train_tree <- predict(tree_model, newdata = train_model, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
  prob_test_tree  <- predict(tree_model, newdata = test_model, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
  #same threshold as before
  threshold_tree <- quantile(prob_train_tree, probs = 0.80, na.rm = TRUE)
  #now we predict the class based on the threshold for the testing dataset
  pred_test_tree <- factor(ifelse(prob_test_tree >= threshold_tree, "Yes", "No"),
                           levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  
  
#finally, we put together all metrics from the models
  metrics_tbl <- bind_rows(
    get_metrics(prob_test_logit, pred_test_logit, test_model$low_perf_c8,
                "logistic", threshold_logit),
    get_metrics(prob_test_nb, pred_test_nb, test_model$low_perf_c8,
                "naive_bayes", threshold_nb),
    get_metrics(prob_test_tree, pred_test_tree, test_model$low_perf_c8,
                "decision_tree", threshold_tree))

  #the output database with everything for simplicity
  out <- list(
    models = list(
      logistic = logit_model,
      naive_bayes = nb_model,
      decision_tree = tree_model),
    predictions = list(
      logistic = tibble(truth = test_model$low_perf_c8,
                        prob = prob_test_logit,
                        pred = pred_test_logit),
      naive_bayes = tibble(truth = test_model$low_perf_c8,
                           prob = prob_test_nb,
                           pred = pred_test_nb),
      decision_tree = tibble(truth = test_model$low_perf_c8,
                             prob = prob_test_tree,
                             pred = pred_test_tree)),
    metrics = metrics_tbl)
  return(out)
}
```

```{r}
#now, we can run the analysis for all the windows of cases in the dataset
#empty list to store the results
results_list <- list()
#now the loop for all windows
for (w in names(window_data_list)) {
  #dataset for the window happening now
  current_data <- window_data_list[[w]]
  #based on the division created before to split data, we split the 
  #data of this window into training and test
  train_df <- current_data[split_index, ]
  test_df  <- current_data[-split_index, ]
  #now that we have the dataset, we do imputation for missing values
  imputed_data <- median_impute_from_train(train_df, test_df,
                                           outcome_name = "low_perf_c8")
  train_df <- imputed_data$train
  test_df  <- imputed_data$test
  #now we run the models!
  results_list[[w]] <- fit_and_evaluate_models(train_df, test_df)
}

#after the for loop, we put all metrics together
all_metrics <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(results_list), function(w) {
    results_list[[w]]$metrics |>
      mutate(window = w)
  }))|>
  select(window, everything()) |>
  arrange(window, desc(balanced_accuracy), desc(accuracy))

all_metrics
```

```{r}
#similar to what I did before
predict_yes_prob <- function(model_obj, model_name, newdata) {
  if (model_name == "logistic") {
    predict(model_obj, newdata = newdata, type = "response")
  } else if (model_name == "naive_bayes") {
    predict(model_obj, newdata = newdata, type = "raw")[, "Yes"]
  } else if (model_name == "decision_tree") {
    predict(model_obj, newdata = newdata, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
  } else {
    stop("Unknown model name")
  }
}

balanced_acc_fn <- function(pred, truth) {
  cm <- confusionMatrix(pred, truth, positive = "Yes")
  as.numeric(cm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"])
}

perm_importance <- function(model_obj, model_name, test_df, threshold,
                            outcome_name = "low_perf_c8",
                            n_perm = 200, seed = 1234) {

  set.seed(seed)

  test_model <- test_df |>
    select(-student_id)

  truth <- test_model[[outcome_name]]
  predictor_names <- setdiff(names(test_model), outcome_name)

  base_prob <- predict_yes_prob(model_obj, model_name, test_model)
  base_pred <- factor(ifelse(base_prob >= threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                      levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  base_ba <- balanced_acc_fn(base_pred, truth)

  importance_tbl <- lapply(predictor_names, function(v) {
    drops <- replicate(n_perm, {
      perm_df <- test_model
      perm_df[[v]] <- sample(perm_df[[v]])

      perm_prob <- predict_yes_prob(model_obj, model_name, perm_df)
      perm_pred <- factor(ifelse(perm_prob >= threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                          levels = c("No", "Yes"))

      base_ba - balanced_acc_fn(perm_pred, truth)
    })

    tibble(
      variable = v,
      importance = mean(drops, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_importance = sd(drops, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    arrange(desc(importance))

  list(
    baseline_balanced_accuracy = base_ba,
    importance = importance_tbl
  )
}
```
